This is a new regulatory development not present in the 2023 Item 7 disclosures, which focus on TCJA R&D capitalization (D067), FDII/stock-based compensation benefits (D066, D068), and general effective tax rate drivers. No 2023 counterpart regarding Pillar Two exists in the required IDs.

current_disclosures.summary: While Pillar Two legislation has been enacted in certain jurisdictions effective for fiscal year 2025, NVIDIA does not expect a material impact on its effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year based on current enacted laws, though new guidance could change this assessment.

materiality_analysis.reason: This is an introduced disclosure addressing the impact of new global minimum tax legislation (Pillar Two) effective in 2025. Although NVIDIA states no material impact is currently expected, the disclosure of a new regulatory regime and the explicit disclaimer that 'new guidance could change this assessment' introduces a new forward-looking risk and compliance consideration not previously present.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure assesses the impact of Pillar Two legislation on the *next* fiscal year (FY2025). In the 2025 filing, FY2025 has passed, so this forward-looking statement is no longer relevant. The disclosure represents a temporal shift in reporting cycles rather than a material change in tax risk or regulatory exposure. The underlying tax environment (Pillar Two) remains, but the specific disclosure about its impact on the upcoming year is naturally removed.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Pillar Two on company's 2024 financials
comparisons.peer_summary: The impact of Pillar Two legislation on the company for the fiscal year 2024 was immaterial, and the company continues to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose that Pillar Two legislation has been enacted in key jurisdictions (EU, UK) with effective dates starting in fiscal year 2025. Both companies conclude that the impact on their 2024 financials and effective tax rate is immaterial/not material based on current enacted laws. However, AMD explicitly states the 2024 impact was immaterial, while NVIDIA projects no material impact for the next fiscal year (2025). Both continue to monitor new guidance.

sentences.text: The OECD has announced an Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting including Pillar Two Model Rules for a new 15% global minimum tax applicable to large multinational corporations.
Based on enacted laws, Pillar Two is not expected to materially impact our effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year.
For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial.
We continue to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes to our effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.

peer_results.rationale: While AVGO has peer candidates (avgo_2024_7_D043 on fiscal calendar and avgo_2024_7_D028 on Singapore tax incentives), neither candidate addresses the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax or its impact on the effective tax rate. avgo_2024_7_D043 concerns fiscal year length, and avgo_2024_7_D028 concerns Singapore-specific tax incentives, which is a different topic from the global minimum tax framework discussed by NVIDIA.

While INTC has peer candidates (intc_2024_7_D152 on factors impacting effective tax rate and intc_2024_7_D096 on valuation allowance), neither provides a specific assessment of the Pillar Two impact comparable to NVIDIA's disclosure. intc_2024_7_D152 mentions Pillar Two only as one of many factors that *could* impact the rate, without the specific conclusion about immateriality/material impact for the current/future year found in NVIDIA's text. intc_2024_7_D096 discusses valuation allowances for deferred tax assets due to historical losses, which is unrelated to Pillar Two.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Tax Legislation Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD Pillar Two legislation is effective for the company in 2025 and is expected not to materially impact the 2025 effective tax rate. However, other countries including Singapore plan to adopt similar legislation effective in 2026, which would significantly increase tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA and Micron both identify Pillar Two as a key OECD initiative with enacted legislation in the EU effective for fiscal year 2025. Both companies state that they do not expect this enacted legislation to materially impact their effective tax rate for the relevant period (NVIDIA for next fiscal year, Micron for 2025). A key difference is that Micron warns that additional jurisdictions, specifically Singapore, plan to adopt similar legislation effective in 2026 which would significantly increase tax expense, whereas NVIDIA notes only that new guidance could change its current assessment.

sentences.text: The OECD has announced an Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting including Pillar Two Model Rules for a new 15% global minimum tax applicable to large multinational corporations.
Certain jurisdictions, including European Union member states and the United Kingdom, have enacted Pillar Two legislation that will start to become effective for our fiscal year 2025.
Based on enacted laws, Pillar Two is not expected to materially impact our effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year.

Further changes in the tax laws of foreign jurisdictions could arise as a result of the base erosion and profit shifting project, including Pillar Two Model Rules ("Pillar Two"), undertaken by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ("OECD").
Nearly all European Union member states have enacted the Pillar Two legislation, which will be effective for us in 2025.

While we do not expect these enacted laws to materially impact our effective tax rate for 2025, additional countries where we operate, including Singapore, have announced plans to adopt Pillar Two legislation.
Enactment of this legislation would become effective for us in 2026 and significantly increase our tax expense.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD announced a framework for a 15% global minimum tax (Pillar Two), with legislation in certain countries set to apply to the company starting in fiscal year 2025. QCOM does not currently expect a material impact on consolidated financial statements but continues to monitor implementation and OECD guidance.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA and QCOM both discuss the OECD's Pillar Two framework establishing a 15% global minimum tax. Both note that legislation is being implemented in certain countries starting in fiscal year 2025. Both companies explicitly state they do not currently expect a material impact on their financial results (NVIDIA: effective tax rate/cash flows; QCOM: consolidated financial statements) from this legislation. Both continue to monitor the situation as countries implement rules and the OECD provides guidance.

sentences.text: The OECD has announced an Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting including Pillar Two Model Rules for a new 15% global minimum tax applicable to large multinational corporations.
Based on enacted laws, Pillar Two is not expected to materially impact our effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year.
New legislation or guidance could change our current assessment.
The OECD has announced a framework to implement a global minimum tax of 15% (referred to as Pillar Two).
Certain countries have implemented or are in the process of implementing the Pillar Two legislation, which will apply to us beginning in fiscal year 2025.

While we do not currently expect this to materially impact our consolidated financial statements, we continue to monitor the impact as countries implement legislation and the OECD provides additional guidance.
